overview: Nasdaq, Inc. operates the Nasdaq Stock Market and a family of exchanges and clearing venues, but has transformed over the past decade into a diversified financial technology and data company. Since closing the ~$10.6 billion acquisition of Adenza (AxiomSL + Calypso) from Thoma Bravo in November 2023, more than half of Nasdaq's revenue is recurring "Solutions" revenue from software, data, and index licensing rather than transaction-based trading fees. The company operates three segments — Capital Access Platforms, Financial Technology, and Market Services — serving exchanges, banks, asset managers, corporates, and regulators globally, with the majority of revenue still U.S.-concentrated but a growing international footprint in financial technology and surveillance software.

business_model.summary: Nasdaq earns a blend of high-margin recurring software/licensing revenue (anti-financial-crime, risk and regulatory technology, index licensing, data and listing services) and transaction-based revenue from operating cash equity, options, and derivatives exchanges plus clearing and market data. Post-Adenza, management's strategic emphasis is on growing Annualized Recurring Revenue (ARR) and shifting the mix toward Solutions (software-like) revenue away from cyclical trading volumes.

revenue_streams.name: Financial Technology (Verafin, AxiomSL, Calypso, market tech)
Capital Access Platforms (Data & Listings, Index, Workflow & Insights)

business_model.customer_type: B2B/enterprise — banks, broker-dealers, asset managers, exchanges, regulators, public and private companies (listings), and institutional investors; minimal direct B2C exposure
business_model.geographic_mix: Predominantly United States, with meaningful and growing international revenue from Financial Technology (AxiomSL/Calypso have large European and APAC bank/regulator client bases) and index licensing globally

competitive_position.market_position: Operator of the second-largest U.S. equities listing venue and a top-tier U.S. options/derivatives market; a leading provider of anti-financial-crime (Verafin) and regulatory risk software (AxiomSL, Calypso) to banks globally; major index provider (Nasdaq-100/QQQ) with AUM benchmarked to its indices surpassing $1 trillion in Q2 2026

moat_factors.description: Operating a national securities exchange requires SEC registration as a self-regulatory organization; high barriers to new entrants in listings and primary market structure

AxiomSL and Calypso are deeply embedded in bank regulatory reporting and treasury/risk workflows; Verafin's AML/fraud detection relies on a data consortium network effect across 2,800+ financial institutions
Nasdaq-100/QQQ brand recognition drives sticky, scalable index licensing revenue tied to AUM growth
ARR of $3.3 billion+ as of Q2 2026 reduces cyclicality versus a pure trading-volume model
Proprietary and tape-plan market data create a durable, high-margin revenue stream

weaknesses: Market Services (cash equities/options) revenue remains volume- and volatility-dependent and competes with low-cost rivals (Cboe, IEX) and ever-rising off-exchange/dark trading volume (>50% of Nasdaq-listed share volume now executes off-exchange)
High financial leverage from the debt-funded Adenza deal constrains capital flexibility versus peers like ICE/CME
Integration risk and goodwill concentration: Adenza-related goodwill/intangibles are a large share of the balance sheet
Facing a formal EU antitrust investigation (with Deutsche Börse) over Nordic derivatives conduct, a reputational and potential financial risk
Newer growth bets (tokenization, 23/5 trading) are unproven revenue contributors and expose Nasdaq to execution and first-mover risk in largely unregulated/nascent markets

growth_drivers: Continued ARR growth in Financial Technology (16% ARR growth in Q2 2026) driven by Verafin cross-sell/up-sell (2,800+ clients, 58 new clients added in Q2 2026) and AxiomSL/Calypso regulatory-driven demand
Index licensing growth as AUM benchmarked to Nasdaq indices surpassed $1 trillion for the first time in Q2 2026, aided by record net inflows
Capital markets activity recovery: record/landmark IPOs (e.g., SpaceX's ~$86 billion IPO) and healthy new-listing pipeline boosting Capital Access Platforms
Extended-hours/23/5 equities trading launch targeted for December 6, 2026, intended to capture incremental trading volume and retail/global demand for near-continuous markets

Tokenization strategy: $100 million Nasdaq Ventures investment in Payward (Kraken's parent) announced September 2026, targeting a 2027 launch of Nasdaq Equity Tokens (NETs) and tokenized-securities market infrastructure/surveillance
Record U.S. options volumes and continued growth in Market Services
Ongoing operating leverage and margin expansion (non-GAAP operating margin reached 57% in Q2 2026, up 2 points YoY) as Solutions revenue scales
Continued capital return acceleration (buybacks, dividend growth) as deleveraging targets are achieved ahead of schedule

business.description: Market Services revenue (~23% of net revenue) still fluctuates with equity/options trading volumes and market volatility, which are cyclical and unpredictable
Off-exchange execution now exceeds 50% of volume in Nasdaq-listed names, pressuring exchange market share and transaction revenue
Large enterprise software deals (AxiomSL/Calypso) carry long sales cycles and implementation risk with big-bank customers
23/5 trading and tokenized securities (NETs) are unproven; adoption, liquidity, and competitive response from Coinbase, Robinhood, and others are uncertain

financial.description: Gross leverage was approximately 4.7x at close (Nov 2023) and has been reduced ahead of schedule (~3.0-3.1x by late 2025), but still above pre-deal levels, limiting near-term M&A/capital flexibility
Adenza-related goodwill and acquired intangibles represent a large portion of total assets; future impairment risk if Fintech growth decelerates
Debt-funded acquisition increases sensitivity to interest-rate levels on floating-rate or refinanced debt

regulatory.description: European Commission opened a formal antitrust probe (announced Nov 2025) into Nasdaq and Deutsche Börse over alleged coordination in Nordic financial derivatives listing, trading, and clearing; could result in fines or required conduct changes
Ongoing SEC rulemaking on market structure, tick sizes, access fees, and extended/24-hour trading rules could alter Nasdaq's competitive and economic position as an SRO
Nasdaq's proposed rule change to enable trading of tokenized securities is still working through SEC review; regulatory delay or rejection would push back the 2027 NET/Kraken launch timeline
AxiomSL/Calypso serve banks navigating Basel, EMIR, and other regulatory regimes; changes to those regimes can be a tailwind or a compliance cost depending on direction

macro.description: IPO activity, index AUM, and listings depend on equity market strength and investor risk appetite; a prolonged downturn would hit Capital Access Platforms and Market Services
Higher-for-longer rates raise Nasdaq's debt service costs following the debt-funded Adenza deal, while also affecting bank customers' technology budgets

As critical market infrastructure, Nasdaq is relatively defensive in downturns (trading volumes can rise in volatility) but a systemic crisis affecting bank customers could pressure Fintech software budgets

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Exchange/fintech data and infrastructure providers are benefiting from secular growth in passive investing (index AUM), rising demand for AML/regtech compliance software, record options trading activity, and early-stage digital-asset/tokenization market infrastructure build-out; IPO markets have reopened materially in 2025-2026 after a multi-year slowdown
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate — Market Services and listings/IPO revenue are cyclical with capital markets activity, but the growing Solutions (recurring software/subscription) mix provides a structurally more stable earnings base than a decade ago
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate — elevated post-Adenza debt load makes interest expense a meaningful line item; rate cuts would aid deleveraging economics and could also stimulate capital markets activity

recent_developments.event: Nasdaq Ventures announced a $100 million investment in Payward (Kraken's parent), deepening a partnership to launch tokenized equities (Nasdaq Equity Tokens/NETs) and always-on market infrastructure, targeting a Q2 2027 launch

Reported record Q2 2026 results: net revenue of $1.5 billion (+15%), non-GAAP diluted EPS of $1.07 (+25%, first time topping $1.00/share), ARR of $3.3 billion (+12% YoY); raised FY2026 non-GAAP opex guidance to $2.530-$2.570 billion
Index AUM benchmarked to Nasdaq indices surpassed $1 trillion for the first time, aided by record quarterly net inflows of $51 billion
Capital Access Platforms benefited from the SpaceX IPO (~$86 billion raised), described by management as the largest IPO in history
Shareholders re-elected Adena Friedman as CEO and Chair of the Board at the 2026 Annual Meeting; no near-term management transition signaled
Nasdaq and Kraken announced a partnership to distribute tokenized stocks globally, preceding the subsequent $100 million Payward investment
European Commission opened a formal antitrust investigation into Nasdaq and Deutsche Börse over alleged coordination in Nordic financial derivatives listing, trading, and clearing in the EEA

Gross leverage reduced to approximately 3.0-3.1x, ahead of the original post-Adenza deleveraging schedule (initial target: 4.0x within 18 months, ~3.3x within 36 months); Nasdaq repurchased ~$69 million of debt in Q3 2025

Nasdaq is preparing to launch 23/5 (nearly round-the-clock weekday) equities trading, targeted for December 6, 2026, as part of broader market-structure modernization alongside other exchanges pursuing similar extended-hours initiatives

items.notes: Increased from prior $2.485-$2.545 billion range, driven by higher performance-linked compensation and increased marketing investment tied to stronger revenue performance
Unchanged across Q1 and Q2 2026 guidance updates

items.target: Continued double-digit growth (ARR was $3.3 billion as of Q2 2026, +12% YoY)
items.notes: Financial Technology ARR grew 16% YoY in Q2 2026, ahead of total company ARR growth, per management commentary

items.target: $200-$250 million accelerated share repurchase program in Q3 2026, plus ongoing quarterly dividend
items.notes: Follows $530 million returned to shareholders in Q2 2026 ($356 million buybacks, $174 million dividends); capital return pace increasing as deleveraging targets are achieved ahead of schedule

guidance.management_commentary: Management emphasized broad-based momentum across all three segments, record options volumes, record index AUM inflows, and continued ARR growth as evidence of a more durable, less cyclical revenue base post-Adenza. Leadership reiterated confidence in growth initiatives including AI-enabled Verafin adoption (750 agentic AI users), the December 2026 launch of 23/5 trading, and the tokenized-securities/NETs partnership with Kraken/Payward targeted for a 2027 launch, while noting opex guidance was raised to reflect reinvestment in growth rather than cost overruns.

bull_case: Successful pivot toward recurring, high-margin Solutions revenue (ARR of $3.3B+, growing double digits) reduces historical dependence on volatile trading volumes and supports margin expansion (57% non-GAAP operating margin in Q2 2026)

Verafin's consortium-data network effect and AxiomSL/Calypso's deep embedding in bank risk/regulatory workflows create durable switching costs and cross-sell opportunities as the Adenza integration matures

Multiple embedded options on secular themes — record index AUM/passive investing growth, reopening IPO markets, extended-hours (23/5) trading, and early-mover position in tokenized securities — offer several avenues for above-market growth
Deleveraging has run ahead of schedule, freeing up capital for accelerated buybacks and dividend growth while still reducing financial risk
Strong, long-tenured management team (CEO since 2017) with a consistent track record of executing the technology-company transformation thesis
bear_case: Elevated leverage from the debt-funded Adenza acquisition leaves less room for error and ties capital allocation flexibility to continued deleveraging progress
EU antitrust investigation into alleged Nordic derivatives market coordination with Deutsche Börse introduces headline, fine, and potential remedial-conduct risk with an uncertain timeline

Core Market Services business continues to face share erosion from off-exchange trading venues (>50% of Nasdaq-listed volume) and low-cost competitors (Cboe, IEX), structurally pressuring the legacy exchange business

New growth bets — tokenized securities/NETs with Kraken and 23/5 trading — are unproven, face regulatory approval uncertainty, and could fail to generate meaningful near-term revenue despite capital and management attention

Valuation reflects high expectations for continued double-digit ARR growth and margin expansion; any slowdown in Fintech bookings or a capital-markets downturn (fewer IPOs, lower index AUM) could compress the multiple
